signal: Alluxio released Enterprise AI 3.6 and 3.7, delivering sub-millisecond latency and model-distribution features to accelerate AI training and inference workloads.

email.body1:
John, saw Alluxio shipped Enterprise AI 3.7 with sub-millisecond latency for AI workloads on cloud storage.

Leaning into the AI-infrastructure wave usually surfaces more strategic accounts than the team can cover before the motion settles, and that is where enterprise deals stall. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Alluxio off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
John, quick follow-up for Alluxio.

As the Enterprise AI line expands, the strategic-accounts target tends to grow faster than headcount can. Most teams cannot say exactly how many meetings they need to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Alluxio needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
John, last bit of proof for Alluxio.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Alluxio's reply rate likely compares to peer data-infrastructure teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
